blocks.text: REQUIRED FIELDS FOR FUTURE LOCATION DEVELOPMENT
Every future location entry should include a Real-world basis, even when the relationship is loose, abstract, architectural, geological, ecological, or metaphorical.
Every entry should identify the World tradition or traditions it most strongly expresses and explain whether that relationship is historical, aesthetic, philosophical, or a later interpretation.

Every entry should connect to at least one established or proposed location through ecology, travel, trade, migration, shared infrastructure, story history, artistic lineage, language, or a disputed resemblance.
Every entry should state its metaphorical function: what relationship, ethical problem, historical wound, form of care, or theory of identity the location makes visible.

Real-world cultures should not be blended as interchangeable decoration. Use a reference for a specific physical or social principle—water management, cliff construction, seasonal migration, public courtyards, acoustic design, forest stewardship, or another concrete relationship.

Abstract locations still need legible sensory anchors. A place can represent memory, distance, translation, or identity while retaining a clear surface, scale, light source, movement pattern, and way ordinary inhabitants live there.
